title: The Gambia calculator readiness — Batch 51
scope: New national crop, input-support, producer-price and mechanisation evidence. Existing five-region lookup is retained; no calculator activation or formula change.

administrative_geography.note: Do not add Banjul or Kanifing to the five-region selector as if they were administrative regions.

2024_2025_crop_area_and_output.source: WTO Trade Policy Review, The Gambia, WT/TPR/G/482, 17 December 2025; Planning Services Unit, Department of Agriculture
2024_2025_crop_area_and_output.caveat: The WTO report presents annual output series to 2024 and 2024/25 cropping-season aggregate area/output. These are national values, not regional crop yields.

2025_output_update.source: 2026 State of the Nation Address reported by The Standard
2025_output_update.reconciliation: FAO GIEWS estimates 2025 aggregate cereal production at about 135,000 tonnes, approximately 20 percent above the five-year average. The 131,798-tonne State of the Nation figure and FAO's 135,000-tonne estimate differ; retain both as separate source estimates pending reconciliation.

current_2026_season.source: FAO GIEWS country brief, reference date 22 September 2026
findings: Planting of 2026 coarse-grain and rice crops was completed in July.
An erratic start to rains delayed planting and germination in several producing areas; replanting was reported in southeastern Central River Region.
Improved rainfall from late July through early September supported crop recovery; satellite vegetation conditions were average to above average by early September.
Final 2026 harvest output and province-level yield tables were not available in the reviewed source.

groundnut.source: Ministry of Agriculture announcement reported by The Point
groundnut.caveat: Season-specific official producer price; not assumed to remain the price for 2026/27.

fertilizer.source: Ministry of Agriculture announcement reported by The Point and The Standard
fertilizer.support: 10,000 tonnes of organic fertilizer planned for free distribution; rice, maize, groundnut, cowpea and findi seed allocations reported.
fertilizer.caveat: Subsidized price per bag is a farmer support price, not the unsubsidized market price. Confirm product grade and bag weight before using in per-kg or per-tonne calculations.

mechanization.source: Gambia Daily, reporting the Agriculture Minister's National Assembly statement
mechanization.caveat: Government service-rate range; private operators in some areas were reportedly charging GMD 7,000–9,000/ha. Not a complete machinery cost schedule.

groundnut_purchases.source: Gambia Daily, reporting the Agriculture Minister's National Assembly statement
groundnut_purchases.caveat: Trade-season procurement volume; not a yield or price observation.

statistical_programme.source: FAO 50x2030 Agricultural Integrated Survey Programme — The Gambia
statistical_programme.findings: The 2025 National Agricultural Sample Census is being supported by FAO; the last sample census was in 2011–2012. Three rounds of National Agricultural Survey are planned from 2026, including crop-cutting and rotating specialized modules.
statistical_programme.caveat: No completed 2025 NASC regional crop tables were found in this review.

blockers: Reconcile the 2025 national cereal totals: State of the Nation reports 131,798 tonnes while FAO GIEWS estimates about 135,000 tonnes.
Obtain completed 2025 NASC and 2026 National Agricultural Survey tables with crop-cutting yields by region, crop and production system.
Obtain dated farmgate prices by crop, grade, quality, region and unit; retain the GMD 38,000/tonne groundnut floor price as specific to the 2025/26 trade season.
Confirm fertilizer product grade and bag weight and obtain actual farmer purchase prices for seed, fertilizer, crop protection and other inputs.
Expand government ploughing rates into complete regional machinery, labour, irrigation, energy, packaging, transport and storage budgets.
Build validated regional enterprise budgets and regression tests before calculator mapping.
decision: Keep The Gambia research-only. The country now has useful national crop, seasonal producer-price and input-support evidence, but no validated regional crop yields or complete enterprise budgets.
